subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Circles, area, perimeter, volume and surface area
Pythagoras, trigonometry and units of measurement

questions.q: What do the interior angles of any triangle add up to?
questions.explain: The interior angles of a triangle always sum to 180°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon?
options: It depends on the number of sides
questions.explain: The exterior angles of any convex polygon always add up to 360°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
questions.explain: Using (n−2)×180 with n = 5 gives 3×180 = 540°.

questions.q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explain: The interior angle sum is (6−2)×180 = 720°, so each of the six equal angles is 720 ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.q: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, co-interior (allied) angles have what property?
questions.explain: Co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary, summing to 180°.

questions.q: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle?
questions.explain: The circumference equals π times the diameter, πd (equivalently 2πr).

questions.q: Which formula gives the area of a circle?
questions.explain: The area of a circle is π multiplied by the radius squared, πr².

questions.q: What is the volume of a cylinder with base radius r and height h?
questions.explain: A cylinder's volume is its circular cross-section area πr² multiplied by its height h.

questions.q: Which formula gives the volume of a sphere of radius r?
questions.explain: The volume of a sphere is four-thirds π times the radius cubed.

questions.q: A circle has radius 5 cm. What is its area (in terms of π)?
questions.explain: Area = πr² = π×5² = 25π cm².

questions.q: For a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse c, what does Pythagoras' theorem state?
questions.explain: The squares of the two shorter sides sum to the square of the hypotenuse.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of 3 cm and 4 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
In a right-angled triangle, the sine of an angle equals which ratio?
questions.explain: By SOH, sine = opposite side divided by the hypotenuse.

questions.q: In a right-angled triangle, the tangent of an angle equals which ratio?
questions.explain: By TOA, tangent = opposite side divided by the adjacent side.

questions.q: How many cubic centimetres are there in 1 cubic metre?
questions.explain: Since 1 m = 100 cm, 1 m³ = 100³ cm³ = 1 000 000 cm³.

questions.q: Which transformation can change the size of a shape?
questions.explain: Enlargement scales a shape by a scale factor, changing its size, whereas the others preserve size.

questions.q: How is a translation of a shape described?
questions.explain: A translation is fully described by a column vector giving the horizontal and vertical movement.

questions.q: Two shapes are congruent when they are the same...
options: shape but not necessarily the same size
size but not necessarily the same shape
questions.explain: Congruent shapes are identical in both shape and size (though they may be reflected or rotated).

questions.q: The locus of points equidistant from two fixed points A and B is which construction?
questions.explain: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is the same distance from A as from B.

questions.q: How many faces does a cube have?
questions.explain: A cube is bounded by six identical square faces.
